headline: High: n8n’s writable, networked workflow engine can amplify Authelia outputs into unsafe actions and compliance exposure by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth outputs, while n8n can ingest workflow inputs and route them through nodes. There is no documented shared clipboard/MCP channel, so direct prompt injection is not proven. The plausible bridge is manual or workflow-fed content, making the pathway possible but not default and with limited blast radius.
conditions: IF n8n workflows pass Authelia-generated text into an AI Agent node or parser without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF Authelia output is manually copied into n8n workflow inputs, attacker-controlled instructions can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Add a fixed allowlist schema for Authelia-derived fields before n8n parses them.
Insert a human review step before any AI Agent node consumes Authelia output.
Strip markup and instruction-like text from forwarded content.
Use separate workflows for authentication metadata and free-form text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to workflow payloads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia handles OIDC/OAuth and broad network egress, while n8n reads and writes the server filesystem and processes whatever the workflow touches. The pair can move authentication-related data into n8n workflows, and n8n may persist or transmit it through integrations. This is a default-configurable leakage path, though the exact sensitive class is not enumerated in Authelia’s profile.
conditions: IF Authelia-derived identity or token data is passed into an n8n workflow, n8n can store or forward it.
IF an n8n integration node sends workflow contents to a third-party service, data can leave the original trust boundary.
mitigations: Minimize fields forwarded from Authelia to n8n.
Disable or restrict integrations that export workflow payloads.
Store secrets only in n8n credential storage, not in workflow data.
Rotate any credentials used in shared workflows.
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention filters on workflow inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and n8n has execute-shell, subprocess, and filesystem write on the server. n8n also supports multiple instances with shared state via datastore and connected systems. If both touch the same mutable resources, concurrent writes or side effects can collide, and the blast radius includes irreversible workflow or server changes. The profiles do not show locking, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or connected system, state conflicts can occur.
IF n8n Execute Command nodes mutate resources that Authelia-triggered flows also depend on, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Separate writable directories per workflow.
Disable Execute Command for shared environments.
Add file- or resource-level locking around shared targets.
Run Authelia and n8n under distinct service accounts.
requires-engineering: introduce transactional coordination for shared external systems.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions and n8n can orchestrate downstream actions through many integration nodes. If n8n treats Authelia output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated auth result can cascade into emails, tickets, or other actions. Because n8n’s tool-use pattern is action-oriented and no verification step is documented, the default pathway is dangerous.
conditions: IF n8n workflow branches on Authelia output without independent verification, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF an n8n node uses Authelia-derived claims to trigger external side effects, errors cascade beyond the pair.
mitigations: Add explicit verification of Authelia outputs before action nodes.
Require human approval for high-impact branches.
Log and compare auth claims against a second source.
Limit workflows to read-only actions until validated.
requires-engineering: implement signed assertions with verification in n8n.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication layer with no data classes listed, while n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and stores secrets in its credential store. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and residency when identity data or secrets flow through n8n. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF identity attributes or secrets are routed through n8n workflows, n8n retention and logging policies apply to them.
IF the workflow processes regulated data classes, n8n’s connected systems may create residency or retention mismatches.
mitigations: Classify data before it enters n8n workflows.
Exclude regulated fields from workflow logs.
Set short retention on execution history.
Use separate credentials per environment.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for each integration.
